ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each ultimate beneficial owner, director, power-of-attorney holder and beneficial shareholder against the Spanish national PEP list, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, European Union consolidated financial sanctions lists, and Spanish MONEYVAL/AMLD obligations. Enhanced due diligence applies where a client is a PEP, where the commercial model uses cross-border fintech payment rails, or where the jurisdiction of origin is a FATF-designated high-risk third country. All screening results must be documented, risk-rated, and retained for at least 10 years under Law 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Mercantile Registry) – Certificación de Denominación Social; application made through the Colegio de Registradores de España portal (www.registradores.org) and supervised by the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory denomination must be written in Latin script using the Spanish alphabet, must be sufficiently distinct from all existing registered names, and must not be misleading or likely to create confusion with previously registered denominations. Foreign words, acronyms and abbreviations are admissible only where they can be rendered in Spanish-language documents without altering the corporate identity, and the denomination must be pronounceable and compliant with Spanish constitutional and legal naming principles.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed denomination, the applicant may immediately submit one or more alternative names to the Central Mercantile Registry. If the Registry refuses registration on grounds of identity, similarity, or prohibited wording, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso potestativo de reposición) before the Central Mercantile Registry, followed by a judicial appeal before the Juzgado de lo Mercantil in Madrid. The appeal must expressly identify the substituted name, provide comparative Registry searches, and contain reasoned submissions that the proposed name does not contravene Article 407 of Real Decreto 1784/1996.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Spanish SL must maintain a registered office (domicilio social) in Spain that is real and suitable for receiving service of legal process and exercising corporate functions. A virtual office may be used for administrative correspondence and mail-forwarding, but a mere virtual mailbox registered as the sole fiscal establishment creates significant substance risks in tax audits, transfer-pricing reviews, and AML/CFT controls. For an outsourced virtual CFO consultancy, the virtual office is acceptable only where the company maintains actual management, decision-making, personnel, and operational infrastructure in Spain; otherwise tax authorities may rebut the Spanish tax residence and deny treaty benefits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – approximately 10% within the first 24 months for a standard low-risk professional-services entity. The likelihood increases to an estimated 25% to 35% if the registered office is exclusively a virtual address with no leased premises, no local employees, and no physical business assets, or if turnover thresholds trigger mandatory tax inspection criteria.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, of 2 July, approving the revised text of the Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Articles 19-24 on incorporation deed and articles of association, Article 22 on registered office, Articles 23 and 24 on registration and publicity, Articles 58-62 on administrators, and Articles 404 and 443 on share capital of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central for name certification and the Provincial Commercial Registry of the registered office for statutory inscription; a Spanish notary public executes the public deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) filed for inscription in the Mercantile Registry (inscripción registral).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 3,000 fully subscribed and fully paid in cash or in kind before execution of the deed; no statutory escrow lock-up is required beyond full payment, evidenced by a blocked bank capital deposit certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the founders unanimously adopt the attached articles of association and subscribe the 3,000 shares of EUR 1.00 nominal value each, fully paid in cash as set forth in the capital contribution certificate. RESOLVED further to designate Madrid as the registered office and to adopt its full address for statutory notices and legal communications. RESOLVED further to appoint [Name Surname] as sole administrator and managing director, granting broad powers to open bank accounts, execute commercial agreements, appoint attorneys, and represent the company before tax, labor, and administrative authorities. RESOLVED that the administrator carry out all filings, publications, and registrations required for legal commencement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for negative corporate name certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Ministry of Justice, online application window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official application for certification of non-identical company name, specifying at least three preferred names. Pay the administrative fee and receive the negative certification evidencing that no identical or confusingly similar company name exists.
required_dossiers: Official negative name certificate application form
Proposed corporate names in order of preference
Administrative fee payment receipt
Identity details of all founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any proposed name is rejected or a conflicting name appears, revise the ordered name list and re-file; a formal refusal may be appealed before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked corporate capital deposit account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Spanish credit institution selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the name certificate, open a temporary account in the name 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada en formación'. Deposit not less than EUR 3,000 and obtain a deposit certificate confirming full contribution and that funds are blocked for use solely in the incorporation and initial operations.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
Draft articles of association
Valid passport or NIE of each shareholder and legal representative
Bank AML/KYC forms and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank questions the source of funds or beneficial ownership, submit corroborating documents such as bank references, sworn declarations, utility statements, or proven origin of funds; choose another authorized institution if compliance clearance is unreasonably delayed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of notarial deed of incorporation and approval of governance instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public in the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders appear before the notary with the deposit certificate and articles of association. The notary verifies legal capacity, payment of share capital, legality of object, and corporate governance provisions, then executes the public deed of incorporation. The First Board Resolution and appointment of administrators are incorporated into the deed or executed as an integral governance document.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
Bank capital deposit certificate
Commercial articles of association draft
Passport or NIE of each shareholder and administrator
Proof of address of the registered office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a legality objection or requests clarifications, correct the articles or append the requested supplementary declarations and reschedule the notarial appointment for a new execution date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for provisional NIF and tax census registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after execution of the deed, submit Form 036 to the tax agency along with a certified copy of the public deed. Obtain the provisional corporate NIF/NIE tax identification number and complete the start-of-activity census declaration for the corporate object.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed first copy
Form 036 or 036 electronic filing
Identity documents of the appointed administrator
Power of attorney if filing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the census declaration is rejected or tax data is inconsistent, correct the form promptly and resubmit electronically; if necessary, secure a formal tax representation agreement to expedite rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of Madrid (or province of the registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a certified copy of the deed, the incorporation registration application, and proof of provisional NIF to the Commercial Registry. The registrar reviews legality, verifies the administrators' powers and registered office, and issues the definitive inscription or a provisional deferred inscription. Publication of essential company data in the BORME official gazette is completed thereafter.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed of incorporation
Application for registration signed by the administrator
Provisional NIF certificate
Bank certificate or proof of payment of any applicable stamp tax on the deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a defect suspension or qualification, comply with the deficiency note within the legal term or contest the qualification before the Commercial Registry supervisory authority and, if necessary, in court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Final NIF and post-registration labor and corporate book formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registry inscription is evidenced, apply for the definitive NIF by presenting the registration certificate. Simultaneously register the company as an employer with the Social Security Treasury, obtain the employer code, and legalize statutory accounting books and board minute books.
required_dossiers: Certificate of definitive Mercantile Registry inscription
Final NIF application and Form 036 update
Social Security employer registration forms
Company constitution book and corporate minute ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If definitive NIF issuance is delayed, rely on the provisional NIF during processing; for Social Security registration refusals, correct the identity of management and workplace address and resubmit the employer census declaration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ayuntamiento of the municipality in which the registered office or place of business is located, acting with the autonomous community economic development department; no separate industrial authority applies because the service is administrative and office-based.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal economic activity declaration (declaración responsable de actividad) or, where required by local ordinance, municipal opening/operation license (licencia de apertura y funcionamiento) for professional offices.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico and the competent environmental authority of the relevant Autonomous Community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — virtual CFO advisory and bookkeeping services are non-industrial administrative services and do not trigger full EIA or environmental authorization under Annex I or Annex II.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste generation; only sanitary sewage discharged to municipal sewer system must comply with local sewer bylaws and Royal Decree 509/1996 on urban wastewater treatment; electronic equipment waste must be managed under Royal Decree 110/2015 on WEEE.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and evacuation certification for office occupancy under Royal Decree 513/2017, structural load and building occupancy suitability certificate from municipal technical services, and mandatory occupational health and safety risk assessment under Law 31/1995 and related workplace regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Pre-incorporation: file Modelo 030 with the notarial draft of the SL deeds to obtain a provisional NIF from AEAT. Execute the incorporation deed before a Spanish notary, pay the corresponding deed and registration taxes, and file the deed at the Registro Mercantil. After registration, file Modelo 036 (Censo de Empresarios) at AEAT to formalize the definitive NIF and VAT/IVA registration, with the final VAT ID shown as ES+NIF. Non-resident incorporators/officers need a NIE or must appoint an AEAT tax representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime exists in Spain; the SL is automatically a corporate taxpayer. Available elections include the group consolidation regime for Spanish groups holding 75% or more of subsidiaries and special joint-venture modalities (UTEs). Hybrid-mismatch and ATAD anti-abuse rules are mandatory and non-elective; no domestic hybrid election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) — Spanish Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No local turnover threshold: VAT registration is compulsory before the first taxable supply in Spain. For intra-EU distance sales by EU suppliers, the special OSS threshold is EUR 10,000; non-EU suppliers have no threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: AEAT uses the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) near-real-time VAT clearance system for taxpayers whose annual turnover exceeds EUR 6,000,000, with electronic transmission of invoice records to AEAT within 4–8 days via authenticated web services/API. Verifactu-certified billing software (RD 1007/2023) is mandatory for software-issued invoices, requiring tamper-proof sequential hash records and accessible AEAT-compatible event logs. Private B2B interoperable electronic invoicing under the Crea y Crece law is being phased in for all Spanish-established businesses; public-sector invoices use Facturae XML.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports to non-EU destinations qualify for the 0% export exemption under LIVA Article 21 if physical dispatch or transport to a non-EU country is evidenced. For cross-border services (fractional CFO and bookkeeping) supplied to a non-EU-established client, the supply is outside the scope of Spanish VAT under Article 69 LIVA place-of-supply rules, thereby producing no Spanish VAT charge; when supplied to an EU VAT-registered client, the reverse-charge mechanism applies and the transaction is not zero-rated locally.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (DUI — Documento Único Administrativo)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from the EU plus proof of customs exit
Commercial invoice or detailed service contract identifying the foreign customer and the actual service rendered
Inward remittance certificate (SWIFT MT103 or bank transfer evidence) showing receipt of non-resident payment
Proof of the customer's non-EU/EU status including, where applicable, a valid EU VAT identification number with VIES confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Ex post AEAT controls verify export evidence; non-compliant claims are reassessed at 21% IVA plus late interest under LGT Articles 26–27 and are subject to penalty scales in LGT Articles 191–192 (50%–150% of the amount, with 150% reserved for concealment or fraud). Fraudulent zero-rating above EUR 120,000 per tax period triggers criminal tax fraud prosecution (Delito contra la Hacienda Pública), public-contract debarment, and retrospective clawback of all claimed credit or refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as national competent authority for monetary policy, financial stability, payment systems, statistics and AML/CFT supervision; regulatory policy coordinated with the European Central Bank and the European Banking Authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain has full currency convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under Articles 63 to 66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There are no general exchange controls, no prior authorisation requirements for profit repatriation, and no differentiated FX approval regime for non-resident investors. Dividend and profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are processed freely by commercial banks once Spanish corporate tax compliance is verified, fiscal representation requirements are met, and any applicable treaty withholding or domestic 19% non-resident withholding tax is settled. Practical hurdles include anti-money-laundering source-of-funds verification, bank de-risking of smaller corporate structures, Form 720 asset declaration obligations for non-resident holdings by Spanish tax-resident directors, and transfer pricing/beneficial ownership substance requirements where the Spanish SL is part of a multinational group.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain does not impose mandatory surrender, forced conversion, or repatriation timelines for export proceeds. Export receivables may be denominated in EUR or in freely convertible or non-convertible currencies and may be retained in domestic foreign-currency accounts or offshore operating accounts. The remaining obligations are statistical and regulatory: cross-border payment operations exceeding EUR 12,500 must be reported to Banco de España under the balance-of-payments reporting framework on the applicable monthly or quarterly cycle; annual declaration of foreign assets over EUR 50,000 per asset class is due by 31 March on Form 720; Intrastat declarations are required for intra-EU goods traffic, and Spanish customs export documentation must be retained as underlying evidence. The statutory expectation is accurate supporting documentation rather than fixed conversion ratios or surrender percentages.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Multi-Currency Operational Account
Multi-Currency Operational Account and Treasury Cash Pooling Account
Operational Account and Trade Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account and Foreign Currency Account
Digital Operating Account and FX Hedging Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High, subject to PSD2 and Banco de España supervision. EEA-authorised electronic money institutions and payment institutions can provide IBANs, multi-currency wallets, payout services and SWIFT-like rails through passporting, but they are not eligible substitutes for a statutory credit institution account when bank confirmation for capital increases or documentary trade credits is required. Cross-border EMIs such as Wise for business may serve payroll to foreign contractors, vendor disbursements, and collection waterfall accounts, but the primary corporate current account for tax, creditor protection, and SL statutory capital contributions should remain at a fully licensed credit institution. Any EMI arrangement must preserve segregated customer funds, include Spanish language and consumer protection disclosures, and cannot offer deposit-taking or credit products.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most tier-1 Spanish banks require at least one physical presence or notarial verification event before account activation. For a non-resident owned SL, the preferred path is a notarised and apostilled power of attorney granted to a locally resident director, authorised signatory, or legal representative, followed by an in-branch interview at the local commercial bank branch. A fully remote account opening is possible for low-risk SLs through digital onboarding, provided the ultimate beneficial owners pass an online video interview, possess qualified eIDAS digital signatures, and submit certified corporate documents. The Bank of Spain expects banks to apply enhanced due diligence for any transaction involving non-resident shareholders, bearer-like structures, or unexplained source of wealth, so the practical mandate is one authentic, verifiable identity event and a signed ownership/source-of-funds declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership above 25% is opaque, layered through multiple intermediaries or holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Spanish commercial registry certificate, UBO declaration in the statutory form, share register extract, ownership chain chart from each intermediary, notarised passports of all natural-person UBOs, corporate article details, certificate of good standing from foreign registries, and written explanation of the commercial rationale for the holding structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed person or family member of a PEP is a shareholder, director, or authorised signatory
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Explicit PEP status declaration, detailed source-of-wealth report, audited or tax-filed financial statements, independent wealth verification, bank statements covering the funding path, notarised employment and business asset documentation, external compliance sign-off by the SL's in-house or external AML officer, and confirmation of no adverse media.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure, offshore parent, or tax transparency concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Economic substance memorandum demonstrating management and decision-making in Spain, group organisational chart, tax residence certificates, certified financial statements, transfer pricing documentation under OECD principles, business contracts showing real operational activity, licensing and professional registrations applicable to fractional CFO advisory, and Form 720 declarations where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, adverse media, or politically exposed counterparties in the trade payment chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated EU/OFAC/UN sanctions screening results, negative news screening for all shareholders and contracting parties, list of client jurisdictions and counterparties with due diligence files, contractual warranties on non-sanctioned involvement, dual-use or export-control classification if services touch restricted sectors, and compliance committee approval memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for initial capital injection, shareholder loan, or subscription of new shares
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original bank transfer confirmation from the remitting bank, remitter's bank statements, audited financial statements of the shareholder, copy of the corporate resolution approving the capital increase, notarised deed of incorporation or capital increase, tax declaration evidencing income or dividend tax treatment, and an accountant's letter explaining the source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multicurrency ledger inconsistencies or unverifiable cross-border accounting records
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IFRS-compliant multi-currency general ledger, transaction-by-transaction reconciliation, intercompany agreement, invoices with full VAT and corporate tax trail, SWIFT MT103s for each inbound flow, FX confirmations, integrated accounting system extract in Spanish or English, and a statutory auditor's comfort letter when needed.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from foreign shareholders are executed by SWIFT MT103 or SEPA for euro-denominated transfers, using the Spanish SL's dedicated capital account in the name of the company at a tier-1 Banco de España supervised credit institution. The payment message should identify the company as beneficiary and reference the notarised capital increase deed. Before wiring, the bank requires the signed investor resolution, notarial deed of capital increase, registered UBO documentation, and Tax ID of the Spanish SL. The transfer is categorised as a direct investment in equity capital for balance-of-payments statistical purposes and must be reported to Banco de España when above the reporting threshold. Funds should not be passed through third-country intermediary wallets, cryptocurrency exchanges, or aggregated EMI virtual accounts. The bank will verify that the source of funds originates from a bank account in the name of the investor or from an audited group treasury, and any loan intermingling must be avoided to preserve clean equity classification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for urgent high-value single cross-border payments, MT202 for interbank cover if required, and SEPA Instant or SEPA Credit Transfer for euro-denominated intra-EU trade disbursements. Documentary trade settlements are executed through Commercial Letters of Credit issued under UCP600, standby letters of credit under ISP98, and independent guarantees under URDG758. For virtual CFO services, typical outbound treasury payments consist of subcontractor invoices, licensing fees, SaaS subscriptions, payroll, and professional fees; each must be supported by a matching invoice, contract, Irish? Malaga? No, by underlying service agreement and an FX conversion confirmation when the beneficiary currency differs. The financial institution must screen all payee names against sanctions and PEP lists before execution. The Spanish SL does not need exchange control approval, but the bank may require a copy of the invoice and, for large non-trade payments, the previously filed balance-of-payments declaration. Use of distributed ledger rails, personal payment cards, or peer-to-peer transfers is not acceptable for statutory disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards between EUR and freely convertible currencies, executed under ISDA or a Spanish master agreement with credit support annex and valuation margin
FX swaps involving simultaneous spot and forward exchange of principal and interest in two currencies for temporary liquidity matching
Cross-currency swaps with actual exchange of principal and interest to hedge long-term intercompany loans or capital exposure
European-style FX options and zero-premium collar structures to protect budgeted cash flows in USD, GBP, LATAM currencies, and emerging market currencies
Foreign exchange swap agreements executed on regulated markets or with required disclosure of underlyings

Non-deliverable forwards permitted strictly where the underlying emerging or non-convertible currency cannot be settled deliverably in the EU and the nominal exposure is documented against a real commercial forecast

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the financial year-end; normally by 30 April for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential administrative penalties and evidentiary disadvantages; repeated non-compliance may contribute to registry compliance issues. No automatic strike-off solely for late book legalization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Preparation and approval of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders for approval; documents subsequently filed with the Provincial Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Directors must prepare accounts within three months after year-end; shareholders must approve them within six months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director liability exposure and delayed statutory filing. Failure to approve accounts prevents timely registry deposit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; normally by 25 July for a 31 December year-end where approval occurs by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure may arise if accounts remain undeposited for one year after the filing deadline. Administrative fines generally range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, subject to statutory calculation rules; registry closure restricts registration of most corporate acts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ultimate beneficial owner declaration accompanying annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry and the Central Registry of Real Beneficial Ownership, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with the annual accounts and updated whenever beneficial ownership information changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or inconsistent beneficial ownership information may delay or reject the annual accounts filing and may create anti-money-laundering compliance exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after financial year-end; normally 1 to 25 July for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without tax payable generally attracts a fixed penalty, subject to reductions. Where tax is payable, penalties are generally 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay, with increased penalties after twelve months and late-payment interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT summary return, Modelo 390, if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed from 1 to 30 January following the relevant calendar year, unless the taxpayer is exempt from the summary return under applicable VAT reporting rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing may result in fixed tax penalties, generally reduced for voluntary correction before tax authority assessment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit generally applies where, for two consecutive financial years, the company exceeds at least two of these thresholds: EUR 2.85 million in total assets, EUR 5.7 million in net annual turnover, or 50 average employees. Audit may also be mandatory for regulated entities, public-interest entities, qualifying consolidated groups, or where required by shareholders or court order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad). IFRS is generally relevant for consolidated accounts of listed groups and may apply in other permitted cases; an ordinary Spanish SL normally uses Spanish GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain has no separate UK-style annual confirmation statement. The company must maintain current beneficial ownership information, report the ultimate beneficial owner with the annual accounts filing, and update the information when ownership or control changes. Each share transfer must be documented and entered in the Libro Registro de Socios; a transfer does not require an annual re-confirmation if no ownership or control change occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Accounting books, including the journal and inventory and annual accounts book
Sole-Shareholder Contract Book (Libro Registro de Contratos), if the company is a sole-member SL
Director appointments, powers, and changes recorded with the Mercantile Registry; Spain does not generally require a separate standalone physical register of directors

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 300-1,200 per year for a commercial registered-office or corporate-domiciliation service; Spain generally does not require a separate resident registered agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 1,500-5,000 for a small non-complex SL subject to mandatory audit; higher fees apply for regulated, consolidated, international, or high-volume businesses

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D and innovation tax credits (up to 25% of qualifying expenses), accelerated depreciation, and SME tax reductions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 - Corporate Income Tax Return, filed electronically via AEAT portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 20 July following the end of the fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before deductions and tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents report Spanish-source income only; claim DTA relief where applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding taxes paid or payable on Spanish-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible WHT on dividends, interest, and royalties; supported by payment certificates

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year losses against current taxable base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Limited to 50% of taxable base annually; carryforward subject to annual limits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 100 EUR per day of delay (maximum 6,000 EUR), statutory interest on late payments, and potential criminal prosecution for evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Treaty Relief Certificate (Form 123) to AEAT with beneficial ownership declaration and DTA evidence to claim reduced rates
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory 19% on royalties and interest; reduced to 0-10% under most DTAs depending on treaty, recipient status, and activity

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 250,000 EUR (local file); 50,000,000 EUR group turnover (master file)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain applies ESR to entities in relevant activities (IP holding, distribution, financing, or certain services) where group thresholds are met; requires adequate local substance to support tax residency and benefits

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file corporate tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission of Modelo 100 within statutory deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of 100 EUR per day (max 6,000 EUR) plus interest and possible criminal liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for tax debts; potential disqualification from management and criminal prosecution

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Related-party transactions without arm's length pricing or missing TP documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment of profits, fines up to 100% of additional tax due, and criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors personally liable for restitution and possible imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold or remit WHT on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines equivalent to 100-500% of evaded WHT plus interest and criminal penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for unpaid WHT; subject to disqualification and criminal sanctions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming tax benefits without adequate economic substance in Spain
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of benefits, back taxes, fines up to 500,000 EUR or more, and criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for tax liabilities; possible disqualification and imprisonment for fraudulent conduct
